title: Quaint Sour British Cod Cornish Pasty
description: A traditional British dish featuring cod in a sour and springy filling, wrapped in a Cornish pasty and cooked in a cataplana vessel, inspired by ttukbaegi earthenware cookware and following ayurvedic sattvic friendly principles
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large bowl, whisk together lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Add the sliced onion, diced potato, and diced swede to the bowl and mix until they are well coated with the lemon juice mixture.
Cut the cod fillets into small pieces and add them to the bowl, mixing gently to combine.
Roll out the puff pastry on a floured surface to a thickness of about 1/8 inch.
Spoon the cod and vegetable mixture onto one half of the pastry, leaving a 1/2 inch border around the edges.
Brush the edges of the pastry with the beaten egg.
Fold the other half of the pastry over the filling and press the edges to seal.
Use a knife to cut a few slits in the top of the pastry to allow steam to escape.
Place the pasty in a cataplana vessel and cook for 25 minutes.
Remove the pasty from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes before serving.
